scope_note: Released feature-film acting appearances by Rishi Kapoor (4 September 1952 - 30 April 2020), whose screen career runs from a child walk-on in his father Raj Kapoor's Shree 420 (1955) to the posthumously released Sharmaji Namkeen (2022). Includes lead, co-lead, supporting and antagonist roles, cameos and guest appearances, appearances as himself, child roles, and his English-language work (Don't Stop Dreaming and Sambar Salsa, both 2007). The spine is the Wikipedia article 'Rishi Kapoor filmography', which is a real article rather than a redirect; its acting table gives 163 rows, of which 160 are kept. Excluded: Ek Do Teen Chaar (1980), Vijay Anand's multi-starrer that was launched, scheduled for 3 October 1980 and never completed, and which the Shashi Kapoor run excluded for the same reason; Apna Ghar (1989), which the Shashi Kapoor filmography marks unreleased and whose role Rishi's own row gives as 'N/A'; and Raj Kapoor (1987), a documentary about his father in which he appears as himself. Also excluded, and not part of the acting table: Aa Ab Laut Chalen (1999), which he directed without acting in, and television, comprising the posthumous documentary series The Romantics (2023). Nine of the 160 films have no Wikipedia article of their own and carry only title, year and character from the filmography table plus whatever non-Wikipedia sourcing could be found: Gunahgaar (1980), Pahunche Huwey Log (1986), Hamara Khandaan (1988), Janam Janam (1988), Naqab (1989), Inteha Pyar Ki (1992), Sadhna (1993), Mohabbat Ki Arzoo (1994) and Jai Hind (1999). Three of those nine are article-less only because their titles redirect elsewhere, and each had to be caught by hand: Hamara Khandaan is a {{Redirect from film}} into [[List of Hindi films of 1988]]; Naqab is linked as [[Naqab 1989|Naqab]], a malformed target with no article under any spelling; and Janam Janam redirects to [[Dilwale (2015 film)#Soundtrack]] because it is the name of a song in that film, which silently attached Rohit Shetty's 2015 film to a 1988 Rishi Kapoor credit until the impossible release date exposed it. All three repairs are session-local and recorded in extract_config.json. Release year is the Indian theatrical year the filmography table and the film articles give. The Body (December 2019) was the last film released in his lifetime. Career phases below are provisional and should be revisited once phase 2 has filled the narrative and score fields.

career_phases.summary: Two appearances, both in his father's films and fifteen years apart. At roughly three years old he walks through the song 'Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua' in Shree 420 (1955), credited by the filmography table as himself but noted as a child artist. His credited debut is as the adolescent Raju in Mera Naam Joker (1970), for which he won the National Film Award for Best Child Artist.

career_phases.phase: Romantic lead debut and first stardom
career_phases.summary: After a two-year gap he takes the lead in Bobby (1973), opposite Dimple Kapadia's debut, and works steadily through the decade in romances and musicals including Zehreela Insaan, Khel Khel Mein, Rafoo Chakkar, the multi-starrer Amar Akbar Anthony and Sargam. About 25 films, and the stretch that fixes the romantic-hero persona the main Wikipedia article names Bobby, Rafoo Chakkar and Sargam among.

His densest decade at about 51 films, and the one that carries most of the titles his public persona rests on: Karz (1980), Prem Rog (1982), Saagar (1985, reuniting him with Dimple Kapadia twelve years after Bobby) and Chandni (1989). The period also holds a long run of guest appearances as a singer or as himself, several of them in songs rather than scenes.

career_phases.phase: Thinning lead roles and a turn behind the camera
career_phases.summary: About 36 films, with the lead roles gradually giving way to older and secondary parts, and several of the decade's titles surviving without Wikipedia articles. He directed Aa Ab Laut Chalen (1999) without acting in it, the one directorial credit of his career and outside the scope of this workbook.

About 22 films, the fewest of any full decade, across which he moves decisively out of leads and into fathers, uncles and authority figures, including Hum Tum (2004), Fanaa (2006), a guest appearance as himself in Om Shanti Om (2007), two English-language films in 2007, and Love Aaj Kal (2009).

career_phases.phase: Late character-actor phase and posthumous release
career_phases.summary: About 28 films in which the supporting and character work becomes the career rather than a coda, among them Do Dooni Chaar, Agneepath, D-Day, Kapoor & Sons (2016), Mulk and 102 Not Out (2018). The Body (December 2019) was the last film released in his lifetime; he died on 30 April 2020, and Sharmaji Namkeen (2022) was released posthumously with his role completed by another actor.
